summary: Democrat Helena Foulkes leads independent Ken Block, who is running without a party label after a past Moderate Party run and a 2014 GOP primary bid, with Republican Aaron Guckian third, per an Oct. 20 Pell Center poll showing Foulkes ahead by 11 points. The race centers on housing costs, taxes, utility bills and trust, with Republicans split over whether Guckian is a spoiler for Block, per WJAR and Rhode Island Current.

issues.why: Foulkes wants 20,000 new homes funded by a millionaires surtax while Block and Guckian call her plan unworkable and offer permitting reform and public land ideas.
Taxes and spending topped voter concerns at 20 percent in the Emerson and WPRI poll.
Block and Guckian back the Algonquin gas pipeline expansion while Foulkes opposes it and favors renewables.
Voter anger over the Washington Bridge closure helped sink Gov. McKee and Block pitches himself as a fixer of state management.
Block proposes restoring cost of living raises for pre 2012 retirees, Guckian pledges budget cuts to pay for relief, and Foulkes wants more cost analysis.

storylines.title: Final debate turns on tax returns and CVS
storylines.what: At the WPRI debate Foulkes pressed Block to release his tax returns, and Foulkes faced questions about a CVS opioid settlement from her time as a CVS executive.

storylines.title: Pell Center poll shows Foulkes up 11
storylines.what: A Salve Regina Pell Center poll had Foulkes at 39 percent, Block at 28 and Guckian at 17, with 13 percent undecided.

storylines.title: Foulkes reveals 3 million dollar income
storylines.what: Foulkes shared summary tax figures showing nearly 3 million dollars in household income and challenged Block to do the same, which he declined, citing business privacy.

storylines.title: Emerson poll shows Block closing gap
storylines.what: An Emerson and WPRI poll had Foulkes at 44 percent and Block at 35, with Block holding the best favorability rating in the field.

storylines.title: Guckian urges Block to drop out
storylines.what: Guckian said Block had zero path forward, and Block replied that Guckian, polling third with about 7,000 dollars on hand, is the one who should quit.

storylines.title: First televised debate on NBC 10
storylines.what: Block and Guckian both criticized Foulkes on housing and opposed truck tolls, while differing over ICE, and Guckian said he would work with the Trump administration.

storylines.title: Foulkes ousts Gov. McKee in primary
storylines.what: Foulkes beat sitting Gov. Dan McKee 62 to 38 percent in the Democratic primary, running on housing and frustration over the Washington Bridge.

events.title: Release your tax returns?
events.prompt: Your opponent is demanding full tax returns days before early voting ends, and the issue led the final debate. How do you handle your own finances?

opts.label: Release everything now
opts.say: Post several years of full returns and challenge every rival to match it.

opts.label: Release a summary
opts.say: Share income totals and tax paid while keeping business details private.

opts.label: Refuse and pivot
opts.say: Call the demand a distraction and steer back to taxes and the cost of living.

events.title: How to fund housing
events.prompt: Housing costs are a top concern, and a plan for 20,000 new homes funded by a surtax on income over 1 million dollars is on the table. What is your housing answer?

opts.label: Millionaires surtax
opts.say: Back a surtax on top earners to pay for 20,000 new homes by 2034.

opts.label: Permitting reform first
opts.say: Speed permits and build on unused public land without a new tax.

opts.label: Cut budget, veterans village
opts.say: Cut the state budget and build a large veterans village near Quonset.

events.title: Gas pipeline and power bills
events.prompt: Utility bills are a top voter worry and the Algonquin natural gas pipeline expansion has split the field. Where do you stand?

opts.label: Oppose, go renewable
opts.say: Oppose the pipeline and push offshore wind and other renewables.

opts.label: Cautious yes
opts.say: Support the expansion with conditions while cutting hidden taxes on energy bills.

opts.label: Build it now
opts.say: Back the pipeline fully and work with the Trump administration on energy.

events.title: Spoiler pressure
events.prompt: A rival is polling third with almost no money and allies are urging a consolidation behind one challenger. How do you respond to the spoiler talk?

opts.label: Ignore it
opts.say: Stay above the fight and keep talking about your own plan.

opts.label: Court crossover voters
opts.say: Pitch yourself as the only candidate who can win and ask the other side to switch.

opts.label: Demand a dropout
opts.say: Publicly call on the rival to quit and say there is no path forward.

endorsements.who: Elaine Pelino, former GOP primary candidate

ads.theme: Hundreds of thousands of dollars in TV and mail attacks aimed at Block.

regions.name: Providence and the urban core
regions.note: Providence and its mill city neighbors are the Democratic base, while the county's western towns lean more conservative.

regions.name: Kent County suburbs
regions.note: Warwick and its neighbors are swing suburbs where a centrist independent like Block can compete.

regions.name: South County
regions.note: Coastal and rural towns split between affluent Democratic shore areas and conservative inland communities.

regions.name: East Bay and Aquidneck Island
regions.note: Well off coastal towns that lean Democratic but include independent minded voters.
